messages.author: 16fb891f5f994003
messages.subject: question about DST
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Hope all is well. 

I noticed that DST didn't seem to apply correctly when analyzing data from UK Biobank. Looks like time gets converted correctly to ET but the dates when daylight savings occur get adjusted to US date/time when DST occurs (DST occurs at different dates in UK vs USA).

Meaning a person that wore the device on March 26 and 27th (DST in UK) doesn't seem to have his DST reflected and instead DST comes up on participants that wore the device on March 12 and 13th when DST takes place in the US. I'm flagging DST by looking at discrepancies in spt and sleep duration amounts.

I might be missing something obvious. Any thoughts/ideas?

Thanks,
Pedro

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] question about DST
parts:
Hi Pedro,

You will need to specify the timezone where the data was collected via argument desiredtsz = "Europe/London". If you do not specify this then the data will be interpreted in the timezone where you are analysing the data.

If the timezone where the accelerometer was configured is a different timezone than where the accelerometer was worn then also specify the configuration timezone with argument configtz. Otherwise leave it in it's default configtz = "".

With kind regards,

Vincent
